status: approved design contract; proposed logical schema, not an applied migration

tables.name: principals
tables.purpose: Authenticated human, service or worker identity
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(auth_user_id) for humans; human principals map one Better Auth user and receive organization role only through organization_memberships. Service and worker principals may use exact grants without a role-bearing membership; any Bakery membership may carry a shared role bundle or role null for grant-only access. Better Auth owns auth user/session/account/verification/OAuth tables from the pinned provider schema.

tables.name: auth_users
tables.purpose: Better Auth provider-owned human login identity and personal profile
tables.providerOwned: Better Auth user table; Bakery configures UUID IDs and optional user.additionalFields for firstName, lastName and title, maps their logical columns, and generates the provider migration rather than forking the core schema
tables.primaryKeyType: uuid (Better Auth configured UUID ID generator)

fields.name: name
fields.description: Account-wide chosen display name. Retain existing values; never infer first or last names by splitting this field.

fields.name: first_name
fields.description: Optional account-wide given name supplied by the user; trim whitespace, accept Unicode, limit to 100 characters and normalize blank input to null. Existing users start with null.

fields.name: last_name
fields.description: Optional account-wide family name supplied by the user; trim whitespace, accept Unicode, limit to 100 characters and normalize blank input to null. A family name is not required.

fields.name: title
fields.description: Optional self-described job title, up to 120 trimmed Unicode characters; blank input becomes null. Presentation only, never an organization role, verified credential or authorization source.

fields.name: image
fields.description: Existing Better Auth profile-image URL, shared across the user's workspaces. Optional absolute HTTPS URL up to 2048 characters, without embedded credentials; null removes the image. Store no image bytes, data URL or expiring credential here.

tables.constraints: UNIQUE(email); provider authentication lifecycle owns this row. first_name, last_name and title are nullable provider additional fields with no inferred backfill; name and image remain the provider's existing fields. Profile writes target only the session's own user and cannot change email verification, membership or privileges. Personal details are account-wide, not organization preferences. Shared name display resolves the canonical auth_users.name; principals.display_name is a synchronized human display cache, not a second editable profile. Safe Bakery projections resolve through principals and never expose provider account/session columns.

tables.name: organizations
tables.purpose: Bakery-owned organization identity
tables.primaryKeyType: uuid (Better Auth configured UUID ID generator)
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(slug); bootstrap may create one Personal organization; organization creation remains authenticated and authorized. Bakery owns this lifecycle and is the canonical FK target. Retained Better Auth organization rows are historical compatibility data only and never a runtime fallback.

tables.name: organization_memberships
tables.purpose: Bakery-owned principal-keyed per-organization membership
tables.primaryKeyType: uuid (Better Auth configured UUID ID generator)
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(organization_id,principal_id); every human, service and worker membership points to one Bakery principal. Human memberships are role-bearing; a service or worker membership may use role null for grant-only access or an Admin/Developer shared permission bundle. Role is per organization and checked live with active status for every protected action. An inactive membership denies organization access even when exact grants remain; membership deletion revokes that principal's organization grants atomically, while demotion alone does not remove independent grants. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: organization_invitations
tables.purpose: Bakery-owned organization invitation lifecycle
tables.primaryKeyType: uuid (opaque invitation ID preserved through compatibility routes)
tables.constraints: Invitation ID remains opaque and stable for the three Better Auth-compatible recipient routes. Email is normalized and recipient matching uses the current authenticated human provider identity, never request-supplied email. Pending and unexpired state is required for acceptance; pending invitations survive inviter demotion, disablement or removal. The inviter principal is retained independently of continuing membership. UNIQUE(organization_id,email) WHERE status = 'pending'; organization and inviter relationships are server-derived and never authority granted by possession of the invitation.

tables.name: installation_administrators
tables.purpose: Deployment administration independent of organization membership
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(principal_id); human principal only. Installation administration grants no organization membership, repository access, execution authority or plugin capability.

tables.name: permission_grants
tables.purpose: Exact organization, operation or external-action authority
tables.constraints: Exactly one of subject_principal_id or automation_definition_id is set. This is an exact capability record, never a role assignment: it has no role column and cannot promote a principal. External actions require action_version, connection and selected resource; into-Bakery scopes bind supported internal targets. No wildcard or prefix inheritance. UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT over subject, direction, capability/version, connection/resource/internal target. Composite FKs keep every target in organization. New actions and resources never expand a grant. Expiry, revocation and policy revision are checked live. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: applications
tables.purpose: Managed product, including Bakery itself
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(organization_id,slug); organization is the ownership root. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: repositories
tables.purpose: Git source identity and application ownership

fields.name: slug
fields.description: Reserved nullable slug field. Migration 0046 enforces only its lowercase format and no uniqueness; #41 may define the explicit caller-supplied slug contract after its grant. Legacy #126 rows may remain null.

tables.constraints: The nullable slug field is reserved for #41's explicit caller-supplied slug contract; migration 0046 enforces only its lowercase format and no uniqueness today. UNIQUE(integration_connection_id,provider_repo_id) is the stable provider identity. Repository name is display-only. The active-profile FK is tenant-bound by organization and profile ID; the API validates that the selected profile belongs to this repository. UNIQUE(organization_id,application_id,id) and UNIQUE(organization_id,id) support composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization.

tables.name: repository_profiles
tables.purpose: Immutable runtime, tests and delivery policy

fields.name: application_id
fields.description: Application scope copied into every profile so observations and execution pins enforce tenant, application and repository identity together. Legacy #126 rows are backfilled before this column becomes mandatory; the insert trigger preserves writers that omit it.

tables.constraints: UNIQUE(repository_id,revision); UNIQUE(organization_id,application_id,repository_id,id,revision,digest) supports observation and execution profile-identity pins; config schema RepositoryProfile; every new profile publish requires config.branches.base to equal the repository's current default branch; an unobserved digest-valid v1 active profile permits a version-matched default-branch PATCH, followed by a newly published matching-base v1 profile that autoactivates; an observed v2 active profile cannot rotate through this path; published contents immutable. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys.

tables.name: repository_profile_observations
tables.purpose: One immutable v2 readiness observation for one immutable profile revision
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(organization_id,profile_id); one full composite foreign key to the matching repository_profiles row enforces the profile ID, repository, application, revision and digest as one identity. The full observation pin key supports exact task/run/job evidence pins. Exactly one immutable observation belongs to one new v2 profile revision. Base SHA is 40 or 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; separate profile and observation digests, payload, source mapping, and readiness are immutable.

tables.name: repository_role_bindings
tables.purpose: Organization/application-scoped role and alias binding to one concrete repository
tables.constraints: Role and alias keys are normalized within the organization/application scope. Duplicate bindings remain legal so the resolver can return durable ambiguity rather than selecting a first row. `archived_at` is the removal path; future resolution excludes archived bindings. Mutable edits use version compare-and-swap; concrete task/run/job pins are not retargeted.

tables.name: conversations
tables.purpose: Shared discussion with an immutable authorization boundary
tables.constraints: Repository conversation: repository belongs to application and current repository read/operate guards apply. NULL repository means organization-wide shared discussion, restricted by current organization membership and explicit grants. Scope cannot change through PATCH. Creation, listing, transcript, events and referenced content use the same boundary. One conversation may originate multiple tasks within its scope. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: messages
tables.purpose: Durable cross-channel transcript
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(conversation_id,sequence); UNIQUE(conversation_id,author_id,client_message_id) NULLS NOT DISTINCT. Lock conversation while allocating max(sequence)+1 and committing message/turn/outbox/events. Human author comes from authentication; internal agent author/session is server-assigned. Replies stay in the conversation. Body <=32KiB UTF-8; immutable server-built CommentContext <=32KiB; no raw secrets/tool arguments. Same client ID with changed payload is IDEMPOTENCY_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH; authorized duplicates return original message/turn. User messages are immutable after send. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: conversation_turns
tables.purpose: Durable admission and outcome of one shared-chat agent request
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(trigger_message_id); trigger is an agent_request in this conversation. UNIQUE(agent_session_id) when set; session belongs to this conversation. Partial UNIQUE(conversation_id) WHERE status IN (active,cancel_requested). FIFO by trigger message sequence. Inngest owns retry/checkpoints, this row owns semantic admission/outcome. Context cutoff frozen on admission; failure is bounded redacted Fault. Terminal state immutable. Requester is trigger_message.author_id; privileges are checked again on admission/effects, never inherited from another participant. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: channel_links
tables.purpose: External thread routing
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(connection,external_channel_id,external_thread_id); authorize Slack identity before accepting steering. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: tasks
tables.purpose: User-visible work and parent epic
tables.executionAdmission: Task creation freezes canonical strict-v1 profile pins with null observation triple, or the complete exact eligible observed-v2 publication tuple. Task edits never repin from the active pointer.
tables.constraints: repository required before executable kickoff; priority 0..100; versioned CAS edits; parent and repository must belong to application; repository profile ID, revision and digest are jointly nullable and, when present, identify one repository profile; an observation pin may be absent only with observation_id, observation_digest and base_sha all null, otherwise application, repository, profile ID, profile revision, profile digest, observation ID, observation digest and base SHA are all required; base SHA is 40 or 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; task observation and profile identity references use same-organization/application/repository/profile composite keys. Migration 0046 adds same-organization observation-owner, profile-identity and exact observation-pin composite foreign keys with ON DELETE NO ACTION DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED; existing profile pins are checked against their complete tenant-scoped identity and the profile-identity foreign key is validated before migration commit. Strict-v1 tasks may carry a complete profile identity without an observation; observation_id, observation_digest and base_sha are independently all null or a complete matching evidence pin. A direct delete of a referenced observation fails at commit under the new deferred pin; pre-0046 ON DELETE RESTRICT profile references can reject a direct profile delete at the DELETE statement. Both referenced rows remain protected by the end of the transaction; whole-organization cascade may remove tenant rows together. Task/conversation scope must agree: a repository-scoped conversation permits only that repository; installation conversations and their linked tasks remain visible only to principals with the installation grant plus any repository grant required for task effects. Creating a task never widens transcript or artifact access. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: task_dependencies
tables.purpose: Executable DAG, not a second job queue
tables.constraints: UNIQUE pair; no self edge; application lock + recursive cycle check within transaction; same application. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: inbound_events
tables.purpose: Host-level verified and deduplicated provider receipt
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(registration_id,external_delivery_id); same identity with a different digest or event kind is IDEMPOTENCY_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH. Raw bytes are bounded, verified and digested before parsing/redaction; an unbound receipt has no organization authority. Per-organization work is represented by inbound_event_routes. No organization_id: installation_id is the verified installation the payload named and stays null when the installation is unknown or the event carries none. Receipts keep a bounded projection, never the body, and expire at expires_at (received_at plus 7 days); a retention sweep deletes expired receipts and their routes, and keeps a receipt while one of its routes is pending, processing or deferred. The receipt statuses are enforced in TypeScript.

tables.name: questions
tables.purpose: Missing information with first-answer-wins
tables.constraints: CAS open->answered; answer validated; kind=approval rows are typed approvals bound at creation to subject, digest, stage scope and policy digest; run admission consumes one with a single conditional update and revoke is its mirror, so exactly one wins; only human principals decide. Later feedback is a new message. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: plan_revisions
tables.purpose: Immutable coordinator plan revisions awaiting or carrying a human decision
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(organization_id,task_id,revision); body and digest immutable (digest = sha256 over task id, revision and body); only status moves.

tables.name: workflow_definitions
tables.purpose: Named workflow catalog
tables.constraints: UNIQUE slug; deactivate blocks new kickoff, current run follows cancellation policy. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: workflow_versions
tables.purpose: Pinned validated executable definition
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(workflow_id,revision); publish validates references, DAG, budgets and registered actions; immutable once published. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: agent_definitions
tables.purpose: Small cloud agent and harness profiles
tables.constraints: UNIQUE slug; no always-running agent process implied. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: agent_versions
tables.purpose: Pinned prompts, harness, model and constraints
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(agent_id,revision); AgentConfig schema; credentials are references; human and machine grants not embedded. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: organization_repository_rule_versions
tables.purpose: Immutable published organization repository rule baselines
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(organization_id,revision); UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; append-only, the application role has no update or delete privilege; config holds {revision, entries}; digest is SHA-256 hex of the canonical JSON of config; created_by is null only for system-published revisions. The application serializes publishers per organization and compares the expected revision before inserting.

tables.name: skill_sources
tables.purpose: Public or local import origin
tables.constraints: Normalized locator; importer uses permitted origins and checked archive paths; no executable mutable URL. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: skills
tables.purpose: Stable skill identity
tables.constraints: UNIQUE slug; built-in skills may have no public source. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: skill_versions
tables.purpose: Immutable skill revision and manifest metadata; no embedded file bytes
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(skill_id,digest); manifest schema includes input/output, license, tools, MCP requirements, compatibility, limits and the exact file inventory (path, mediaType, sizeBytes, sha256, isExecutable). Digest covers the canonical manifest, excluding storage keys. Publish only after every file has been durably written and verified; draft versions cannot be pinned. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: skill_files
tables.purpose: Skill file metadata; bytes live in private R2 or the local filesystem
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(skill_version_id,path); generated object_key identifies immutable bytes in the installation-selected store, never a public URL. Safe relative POSIX paths only; reject traversal, links and normalized/case-fold collisions. At most 256 regular files and 10MiB decoded bytes per revision. Published file metadata is immutable. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: integration_providers
tables.purpose: Deployment registry for native and later packaged integration contracts
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(slug,adapter_version); immutable manifest digest and complete bounded JSON Schemas for config, actions, outputs and events. Registry JSON is data, never executable code. GitHub and Slack are bundled native entries; public integration packages wait for SDK/sandbox acceptance.

tables.name: integration_connections
tables.purpose: Organization binding to a host-owned provider installation
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(organization_id,id); FK(installation_id,external_authorization_id,external_account_id) to the installation identity so they must agree; external_account_id has no update grant, and installation_id with external_authorization_id may move only together when a same-account reinstall reconnects the connection, so the key keeps it on an installation of the same account. One live connection per (organization_id, installation_id) where archived_at is null. Generic config cannot change secrets or URLs. Disable blocks this organization only; installation revoke blocks all dependent connections. Composite FKs constrain secret and all children to organization where applicable. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: ticket_requests
tables.purpose: Immutable ticket admission generation and authority evidence
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(ticket_task_link_id,generation). external_ticket_id must match the link (composite FK on organization, ticket and link). Partial UNIQUE(external_ticket_id) for waiting/admitted/active/suspended prevents parallel admission; terminal generations free it. Admission locks ticket/link/task and records the exact source policy revision, a pinned readiness report and a pinned preset; it stores no plan artifact version (the API field planArtifactVersionId is always null). origin, authority_principal_id, authority_evidence, inbound_event_route_id and pinned_preset have no update grant; a re-pin rewrites requirements_digest, readiness_report_id and source_policy_revision, and a lifecycle step rewrites intent, disposition, disposition_reason, workflow_run_id and pause_requested_at. Receipt retention sets inbound_event_route_id to null and authority_evidence keeps the durable facts. No delete grant. Vocabulary and transitions are enforced in TypeScript. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: ticket_readiness_reports
tables.purpose: Immutable readiness evaluation of one external ticket for one observed basis
tables.constraints: Insert-only: bakery_app has select and insert and no update or delete grant, so a recorded evaluation cannot be rewritten. Inherits only id and created_at; version is the per-ticket report sequence, not a concurrency counter, and there is no updated_at. UNIQUE(external_ticket_id,version). A new report is stored only when its basis_digest differs from the newest one of the ticket. checks holds one entry per check id with status pass, wait or reject, a reason code and bounded evidence; verdict follows from the checks. origin names the call that first saw the basis. UNIQUE(organization_id,external_ticket_id,id) lets ticket_requests pin a report of its own ticket. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: ticket_task_links
tables.purpose: Explicit same-organization link between an external ticket and Bakery task
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(organization_id,external_ticket_id,task_id); one primary ticket per task. Linking does not start work or widen audiences. A partial unique request constraint owns nonterminal execution per external ticket. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: external_tickets
tables.purpose: Bounded current snapshot of a provider-owned ticket
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(organization_id,ticket_source_id,external_ticket_id); remote identity is independent of URL or connection credential. Snapshot and schema are bounded; attachments remain remote through the selected adapter. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: ticket_sources
tables.purpose: Authorized external ticket container, mapping and versioned intake policy
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(organization_id,integration_connection_id,external_container_id); one authoritative source per external container in an organization. provider defaults to github. Policy is strict data, never executable code or an arbitrary URL. Identity columns (provider, connection, resource, application, repository, external container) have no update grant; the poll writes only sync_checkpoint, sync_health, last_synced_at and last_problem_code, never version or policy_revision. No delete grant. Every parent is constrained to organization. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: external_identity_links
tables.purpose: Verified external human identity scoped to one organization and provider installation
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(organization_id,provider_registration_id,identity_scope,external_user_id). Principal must be a current organization member when used. No raw proof token, handle, display name or email resemblance establishes authority. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: integration_event_subscriptions
tables.purpose: Organization-owned safe event projection and destination policy
tables.constraints: Source and destination resources belong to the same organization and selected connections. Creation is disabled; activation rechecks events:subscribe, underlying reads, exact destination action grant, sender, provider permissions and budget. Policy changes never retarget existing effects. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: inbound_event_routes
tables.purpose: Per-organization authorized processing of a host receipt
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(inbound_event_id,connection_id,purpose); UNIQUE(organization_id,id); FK(organization_id,connection_id) to integration_connections(organization_id,id), FK(connection_id,installation_id) to integration_connections(id,installation_id) (ON UPDATE CASCADE so a same-account reconnect moves the route with its connection) and FK(resource_id,connection_id) to integration_resources(id,connection_id), all ON DELETE CASCADE. A plain btree index on (connection_id, installation_id) backs the cascading key, so a reconnect does not scan the table. Routing derives from verified installation/resource bindings. Each item rechecks organization grants independently; raw cross-organization payloads are never organization-readable. The route lifecycle, attempt bound and retry timing (attempts, not_before) are enforced in TypeScript. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: integration_resources
tables.purpose: Discovered organization-selected provider resource or webhook destination
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(connection_id,kind,external_id); UNIQUE(organization_id,id); FK(organization_id,connection_id) to integration_connections(organization_id,id) and FK(connection_id,installation_id) to integration_connections(id,installation_id), so a resource always shares its connection's organization and installation; no update grant covers those columns, kind or external_id. Setup records only repositories the connecting user administers, available and unselected; a scan that fails or is cut short records nothing. Complete successful discovery may mark unavailable; partial scans do not. URL identity is immutable and uses the approved DNS/IP/redirect policy. Selected GitHub repositories are exclusive across active connections backed by one installation. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: integration_remote_facts
tables.purpose: Bounded provider fact (issue or check run) observed from a fresh provider read; pull requests are stored in pull_requests
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(resource_id,kind,external_id); UNIQUE(organization_id,id); FK(organization_id,connection_id) to integration_connections(organization_id,id), FK(connection_id,installation_id) to integration_connections(id,installation_id) (ON UPDATE CASCADE) and FK(resource_id,connection_id) to integration_resources(id,connection_id), all ON DELETE CASCADE, so a fact shares its resource's connection, organization and installation and disappears with them. A plain btree index on (connection_id, installation_id) backs the cascading key, so a reconnect does not scan the table. A write comes only from a fresh provider read and replaces the stored row only when the (provider_updated_at, observed_started_at) pair is greater and the digest differs. A later-started read of the state already stored leaves the state, digest and version alone and moves only the read clock (observed_started_at and observed_at); an equal or older read changes nothing. A check run has no updated_at, so its provider_updated_at is completed_at, else started_at. The summary is bounded (2 KiB) and carries no issue body. Absence from a list or a partial scan never marks a fact gone. Facts are never deleted by the application. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: integration_sync_checkpoints
tables.purpose: Resumable reconciliation progress for one repository resource and stream
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(resource_id,stream); UNIQUE(organization_id,id); FK(organization_id,connection_id) to integration_connections(organization_id,id), FK(connection_id,installation_id) to integration_connections(id,installation_id) (ON UPDATE CASCADE) and FK(resource_id,connection_id) to integration_resources(id,connection_id), all ON DELETE CASCADE. A plain btree index on (connection_id, installation_id) backs the cascading key, so a reconnect does not scan the table. One row per selected, available repository and stream. The cursor is committed after each provider request so a failed or capped scan resumes where it stopped; a partial scan concludes nothing about items it did not read. Claims are row-locked (skip locked) and ordered by last_completed_at, never before not_before. The status, cursor shape and scheduling are enforced in TypeScript. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: integration_auth_attempts
tables.purpose: Single-use provider authorization and reconnect handoff
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(state_hash); state is single-use and atomically claimed before exchange. The PKCE verifier is AES-GCM ciphertext bound to organization, attempt, state hash and key id; the raw state and verifier are never stored. UNIQUE(organization_id,initiating_principal_id,idempotency_key_hash): a same-key retry rotates state and verifier on the same attempt instead of storing a replayable response. (organization_id,initiating_principal_id) references organization_memberships(organization_id,principal_id) on delete cascade, so removing a member removes their attempts. Callback data cannot choose organization; membership is rechecked before binding. Short retention; no proof token or OAuth code is returned. verified_installation_ids and discovered_repositories (administered repository identities per completely scanned installation) hold callback results until the bind and are cleared when the attempt completes or fails; the provider user token is never stored. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: integration_installations
tables.purpose: Host-owned provider authorization shared by organization connections
tables.constraints: No organization_id. UNIQUE(registration_id,external_authorization_id); UNIQUE(id,external_authorization_id,external_account_id) lets connections pin the identity; external authorization and account ids are immutable (no update grant). credential_secret_id must reference a secrets row owned by this installation. Shared refresh, quota and lifecycle serialize here; every use still checks the requesting organization connection/resource/grant.

tables.name: integration_app_registrations
tables.purpose: Installation-owned provider app registration and its encrypted credential references
tables.constraints: No organization_id. UNIQUE(provider): one registration per provider per installation. The client secret, private key and webhook secret are installation-owned secrets rows (organization_id and application_id null) whose secret_versions hold AES-GCM ciphertext bound to the installation scope; this table stores only their ids; webhook_secret_id is null when the App has no webhook secret. Credentials are configured through the product UI (manifest flow or pasted existing-App credentials), never deployment environment variables. Replacing a credential adds the next secret_versions revision and moves active_version_id; earlier revisions are kept for audit. Read projections expose configured flags and active revision numbers only.

tables.name: integration_app_registration_attempts
tables.purpose: Single-use, session-bound GitHub App manifest registration handoff
tables.constraints: No organization_id. UNIQUE(state_hash); the raw state is never stored. consumed_at is set by one conditional update that also matches the initiating principal, the browser session and an unexpired expires_at, before the provider code is converted; replay, expiry and cross-session use claim nothing. external_app_id and slug record a converted App even when storing it failed, so an administrator can remove the orphan on GitHub. Short retention; no code, token or credential is stored.

tables.name: skill_storage_settings
tables.purpose: Single installation row naming the active skill object storage backend and the saved R2 account and bucket
tables.constraints: No organization_id. One row, id installation, enforced in TypeScript. bakery_app has column-scoped INSERT and UPDATE that exclude backend and endpoint_override, so backend takes its filesystem default on the first row. backend is filesystem until the paused copy, verify and switch procedure writes r2; saving settings never changes it. The R2 access key id and secret access key are one installation-owned secrets row (organization_id and application_id null) whose secret_versions hold AES-GCM ciphertext bound to the installation scope; this table stores only its id. account_id and bucket are validated and the endpoint is pinned to the account's r2.cloudflarestorage.com host; endpoint_override is a loopback fixture endpoint honoured only when BAKERY_ENV is test and is never written by the application. version is the If-Match precondition and the cache key every running store compares on each operation, so a credential rotation or backend switch applies without a restart. No credential value is stored in clear, returned, logged or audited.

tables.name: mcp_servers
tables.purpose: External server definition
tables.constraints: UNIQUE slug; stdio command allowlisted/pinned; no direct shell interpolation. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: mcp_connections
tables.purpose: Configured external MCP with host locality
tables.constraints: Local stdio must declare host or required host capability; localhost endpoints refer to that host, not cloud loopback. Typed config.auth records OAuth issuer, clientId, resource and granted scopes; tokens/refresh credentials reside only in encrypted secret versions referenced by secret_id. Registration and token state are bound to this connection and issuer; changing issuer requires reauthorization, never token reuse. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: mcp_capability_snapshots
tables.purpose: Discovered tools/resources/prompts and schema digests
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(connection_id,digest); discovery cannot auto-grant a new tool; schema drift requires re-resolution. Record the actually observed protocol_version; Bakery targets 2026-07-28 and does not claim old upstream versions are compatible. No MCP session identity is persisted. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: capability_bindings
tables.purpose: FK-backed ownership and target assignment
tables.constraints: CHECK exactly one owner FK and exactly one target FK; step_key requires workflow owner; no unvalidated polymorphic ids; bindings immutable with versioned owners. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: secrets
tables.purpose: Stable credential reference and policy
tables.constraints: Exactly one owner is set: organization_id XOR integration_installation_id. Organization-owned secret references use composite same-organization FKs; host integration credentials may be read only by the central broker for the owning installation. Secret values never appear in projections, logs or generic config. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports tenant composite FKs. Project APIs require non-null same-organization application ownership and exclude installation rows. TypeScript owns ownership/policy/counter validation; SQL stores relational structure only.

tables.name: secret_versions
tables.purpose: Encrypted credential bytes
tables.constraints: Owner columns exactly match the parent secret. Organization-owned versions use the composite same-organization FK; installation-owned versions are accessible only through the central broker. Ciphertext is AES-GCM with external master key; version is immutable and secret bytes are never projected.

tables.name: automation_definitions
tables.purpose: Scheduled or event-driven jobs
tables.constraints: UNIQUE slug; active version changes schedule cursor transactionally. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: automation_versions
tables.purpose: Pinned trigger and workflow inputs
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(automation_id,revision); cron+IANA timezone or registered event predicate, never executable expressions. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: automation_firings
tables.purpose: Deduplicated schedule occurrence
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(automation_version_id,scheduled_at); event triggers additionally UNIQUE(automation_version_id,trigger_event_id); UTC instant handles repeated DST hour. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception. skipped_count >= 0 records missed occurrences; API pending is derived as status = queued and is not separately mutable.

tables.name: workflow_runs
tables.purpose: Pinned run and domain-visible execution state
tables.executionAdmission: Repository run admission revalidates the task's frozen tuple and saves authorized organization/application/repository identity, canonical config and all six pins in the snapshot and relational columns. Completed receipt/attempt authority is historical, not a current inspector lease. TypeScript data migration 0049, registered in workDataMigrations and consumed by migrateData after published SQL in src/tasks.ts migrate/startup, expands only canonical strict-v1 contexts with exact same-tenant task/run/profile and published fixed workflow identity. Atomic batches examine at most 100 rows; interrupted scans are idempotent and completion is recorded only after both phases finish. Original config/id/revision/digest are preserved; the active pointer is never consulted. No SQL data backfill or empty schema migration exists. Cloud/null contexts are unchanged; runtime accepts only the single complete context shape.
tables.constraints: UNIQUE active run per task; snapshot holds immutable config/skill refs + base commit, not granted authority; Inngest owns checkpoint scheduling. Non-repository automation/import runs may omit repository profile; repository execution cannot. Migration 0046 adds same-organization application and repository owner, profile-identity, observation-owner and exact observation-pin composite foreign keys, all with ON DELETE NO ACTION DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED; legacy runs with a profile are checked and backfilled from their matching same-organization task and profile, mismatches are rejected, and the profile-identity foreign key is validated before migration commit. A direct delete of a referenced observation fails at commit under the new deferred pin; pre-0046 ON DELETE RESTRICT profile references can reject a direct profile delete at the DELETE statement. Both referenced rows remain protected by the end of the transaction; whole-organization cascade may remove tenant rows together. Strict-v1 runs may carry complete application, repository, profile ID, revision and digest identity with observation_id, observation_digest and base_sha all null; null-profile non-repository runs retain null identity fields. Profile identity is all absent or all present; a v2 observation pin requires the complete application, repository, profile ID, revision, digest, observation ID, observation digest and base SHA tuple, with base SHA 40 or 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: run_steps
tables.purpose: Stable semantic node attempts in a workflow
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(run_id,step_key,iteration); output stores refs/small typed summaries, not a duplicate artifact body; Inngest retries not new logical nodes. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: agent_sessions
tables.purpose: Cloud or worker harness conversation segment
tables.constraints: Resume ref bound to host + harness version + workspace revision, encrypted when sensitive; human-facing task is not a session. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: jobs
tables.purpose: Work waiting for compatible worker capacity
tables.executionAdmission: Workflow admission and claims require matching job/run/task/snapshot identity and immutable profile/observation evidence. input.repositoryProfile freezes the authorized context. Requirements retain registered action capabilities, existing stricter capabilities/platform constraints and metadata, and add only required observed policy tools plus Linux; request capabilities cannot broaden persisted enrolled host authority. Optional missing tools do not block eligible jobs. Bounded TypeScript data migration 0049 uses migrateData after published SQL in src/tasks.ts migrate/startup to establish only canonical strict-v1 job contexts and absent legacy identity from the exact same-tenant published fixed workflow run-step/run. Registered local action metadata supplies missing capabilities; original config/pins, input/requirement extras and saved encrypted claim replays, attempts, fences and journal digests remain untouched. Cloud/null contexts are not transformed. Jobs/job_attempts have no input digest; claim replay request_digest hashes the claim request, not job input. Corrupt config/digest is denied before migration mutation and independently at runtime.
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(run_step_id,action); Inngest materializes job once, workers pull jobs; no Redis queue. Repository may be absent only for explicitly registered non-code host actions such as MCP discovery. Migration 0046 adds same-organization application, repository, repository-profile, profile-identity, observation-owner and exact observation-pin composite foreign keys, all with ON DELETE NO ACTION DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED; existing non-null profile identities are checked against their complete tenant-scoped tuple and the profile-identity foreign key is validated before migration commit. A direct delete of a referenced observation fails at commit under the new deferred pin; pre-0046 ON DELETE RESTRICT profile references can reject a direct profile delete at the DELETE statement. Both referenced rows remain protected by the end of the transaction; whole-organization cascade may remove tenant rows together. Legacy repository-only jobs may retain repository_id while application_id, repository_profile_id, repository_profile_revision, repository_profile_digest, observation_id, observation_digest and base_sha remain null; strict-v1 jobs may carry complete application, repository, profile ID, revision and digest identity without an observation. Profile identity is all absent or all present; an observation pin is independently all absent or the exact complete matching identity and observation ID, observation digest and base SHA tuple, with base SHA 40 or 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: worker_hosts
tables.purpose: Machine identity and declared toolchain capacity
tables.constraints: UNIQUE principal; slots >0; host capability inventory validated; no provider/model secret values. Credential hash is private; generation starts at 1 for base-compatible protocol v1 hosts and at 0 with a null session for protocol v2 hosts; protocol_version is the negotiated worker contract. A v2 initial heartbeat proposes a UUID with generation 0 and atomically receives generation 1. worker_session_generation is a server-issued monotonic process fence and worker_session_id identifies the currently accepted process session. Revocation/rotation invalidates prior bearer credentials atomically. The worker generates and sends the credential once during registration; Bakery stores only its hash and never returns the credential in a response. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: job_attempts
tables.purpose: Fenced execution lease and recovery truth
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(job_id,attempt_no); UNIQUE(job_id,fence); one live attempt per job; completion requires current fence, active lease and matching host. worker_session_id and worker_session_generation preserve the process session that claimed the attempt while allowing a replacement process to report it after restart with the current server-issued session fence. started_at records the first accepted execution start; last_event_seq defaults to 0; first accepted event is 1; all event/result submissions share one contiguous journal ingestion transaction. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: prepared_operations
tables.purpose: One-attempt server-only fixed credential operation authority and terminal safe result
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(organization_id,attempt_id) and UNIQUE(organization_id,job_id,attempt_id) admit one operation per claimed attempt. Composite foreign keys bind the run/step/job/attempt/worker-session chain and the organization/application/repository/profile/secret/version scope. Database checks enforce provider=github, action=identity.read, SHA-256 digests, 30-second lease-bounded expiry, status/io_attempt lifecycle coherence, a 1,024-byte strict safe-result envelope, bounded account/login/code values, and one I/O admission. No credential, ciphertext, key, bearer, or raw provider response is stored.

tables.name: attempt_events
tables.purpose: Idempotent worker journal ingestion
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(attempt_id,local_seq); UNIQUE(attempt_id,event_id); duplicates identical accepted, changed payload rejected; redacted <=32KiB/event. saved_ack is bounded to 8KiB, written with the semantic event transaction and replayed byte-identically after lease expiry; it contains no credential. Clients only advance their acknowledged prefix monotonically. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: workspaces
tables.purpose: Prepared worktree and cleanup lifecycle
tables.constraints: Paths validated beneath worker workspace root; no reuse of live/lost workspace until process termination is proved. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: previews
tables.purpose: Authenticated dev URL registration
tables.constraints: UNIQUE route_key; port 1024..65535; private origin, separate preview origin, session-bound access, no API cookies forwarded. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: artifacts
tables.purpose: Named task evidence document
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(task_id,name); content in artifact_versions, not Git. pinned_at and pinned_by are both null or both non-null. Pin/unpin, evidence-reference writes and purge share artifact/version locks so the purge guard is atomic. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: artifact_versions
tables.purpose: Immutable evidence bytes and source revision
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(artifact_id,revision); <=10MiB/version; SHA-256 enforced at ingress; HTML/SVG never render in the application origin (previews: separate origin, script-less CSP sandbox); images/patches also stored here. Repository file imports carry validated sourceRepositoryId/path/commitSha metadata and immutable bytes; source repository must match task scope. Publishing a new current version uses artifact If-Match so concurrent editors cannot overwrite a revision. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception. Trusted policy computes expires_at (defaults: transient 30 days, evidence 180 days). content may be null only when purged_at is non-null; metadata, size, digest and every FK/reference row remain as a tombstone. The chapter 14 protected-reference matrix is canonical: the locked purge guard checks relational FKs plus pinned typed input/output references, and requires expired bytes, a terminal task, an unpinned parent, no active run/step, no retained check/review/decision/deployment/health/evaluation/memory evidence, and no unresolved comment. Audit/usage rows, expired or resolved comment metadata, and a terminal task current-version pointer preserve tombstones but alone do not retain bytes.

tables.name: artifact_comments
tables.purpose: Shared version-pinned discussion roots and flat replies
tables.constraints: Root: root_id NULL, status open/resolved, optional typed CommentAnchor. Reply: root_id references a root in the same artifact version, anchor/status/resolved_by/resolved_at NULL. Flat threads only. Root resolution stores actor/time; reopening clears them. Body <=10KiB UTF-8; author is authenticated principal. Author edits own body or soft-deletes/restores; Admin may moderate; permitted Developers resolve/reopen roots. All PATCHes require If-Match. New replies and every reply edit/delete/restore increment root version atomically, including on resolved threads; never auto-reopen. Soft-deleted bodies are redacted in reads/context, root tombstones preserve replies. Original version and anchor are immutable; derived placement never silently retargets history. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: artifact_preview_grants
tables.purpose: One-use, 30 second handoff grants to render one immutable artifact version on the isolated preview origin
tables.constraints: One-use browser handoff to the isolated artifact preview origin, an artifact-scoped sibling of preview_grants. The grant secret is 32 random bytes, base64url; only its sha256 is stored (token_hash), the secret leaves the server once in the create response and is never stored in a replayable idempotency body, audit record, event or log. expires_at is created_at plus 30 seconds. consumed_at is set by one conditional update that also matches an unexpired, unrevoked grant, so a replay or race wins at most once; the secret travels only in a POST form body, never in a URL. revoked_at ends the grant and every session it opened. Every preview request re-checks the grantor's live read authority and the version's tombstone state in TypeScript, so a removed membership or a purged version ends access without a revoke call. UNIQUE(token_hash); UNIQUE(organization_id,id); FKs (organization_id,task_id) to tasks, (organization_id,artifact_id) to artifacts and (organization_id,artifact_version_id) to artifact_versions all cascade; index(expires_at).

tables.name: artifact_preview_sessions
tables.purpose: Short-lived HttpOnly sessions opened by exchanging an artifact preview grant
tables.constraints: Session opened by exchanging one preview grant on the preview origin. id is the non-secret public id carried in the view path; the cookie secret is 32 random bytes, base64url, stored only as session_hash (sha256). The HttpOnly cookie is host only, SameSite=Lax and scoped by Path to its own view path (/artifact-preview/view/{id}), so several previews coexist; https uses the __Secure- prefix because __Host- would force Path=/. expires_at is at most five minutes after creation. revoked_at is set with the grant's. UNIQUE(session_hash); FK(organization_id,grant_id) to artifact_preview_grants cascades; index(expires_at).

tables.name: memory_entries
tables.purpose: Stable repository-scoped learning
tables.constraints: Search by repo+status+tags and text index; no global cross-repo retrieval by default. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: memory_revisions
tables.purpose: Sourced, reversible learning content
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(memory_id,revision); confidence is model judgment, not factual proof; promotion requires provenance validation + conflict scan. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: pull_requests
tables.purpose: Remote PR identity and current SHAs
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(repository_id,provider_number); webhook updates reconciled against provider current state. The observation columns stay null until the first provider read; a read replaces the row only when its (provider_updated_at, observed_started_at) pair is newer than the stored pair, so a delayed or reordered delivery never overwrites newer state. Task and repository references are NO ACTION and the organization reference cascades, so only an organization delete removes a pull request. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: review_cycles
tables.purpose: One independent review of one exact candidate, with the provenance of who reviewed what
tables.constraints: Immutable evidence: the application role holds SELECT and INSERT only, so a row is never updated or deleted, and it carries `created_at` but no `updated_at` or `version` (the read projection reports `version` 1 and `updatedAt` equal to `createdAt`). One row is written by the `review.independent` result transaction after the server verified the report against its own pins; a refused report writes nothing. `ordinal` counts the run's cycles from 0 and is UNIQUE(organization_id,run_id,ordinal). Only `approved` (no blocking finding) and `changes_requested` are written; `running` and `failed` stay in the vocabulary for later writers, and a review job that fails records a stop decision with no cycle. `head_sha`, `base_sha` and `policy_digest` are the candidate the review judged, derived from the review job's own pins and equal to what the report echoed; an approval never applies to another head, base or policy. Independence is recorded, not assumed: `reviewer_session_id` is the review step's own server-created session (never an implementing session of the run, with no parent and no resume), `reviewer_principal_id` is the worker principal that held the attempt, and `implementer_session_id` and `implementer_principal_id` name the latest harness step the review judged. The two principals may be equal (the same host may implement and review); what the row guarantees is a fresh, distinct session. `job_id`, `attempt_id` and `fence` are provenance written by the result transaction without foreign keys, as in `check_runs`, and a partial UNIQUE(organization_id,job_id,fence) where job_id is not null records one cycle per job attempt. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; FK(organization_id,run_id) to workflow_runs(organization_id,id) and FK(organization_id,reviewer_session_id) and FK(organization_id,implementer_session_id) to agent_sessions(organization_id,id) cascade with the run. `pull_request_id` and `artifact_version_id` are omitted until a run has a pull request (#97) and a writer sets them (`pull_requests` has a table now); the `ReviewCycle` projection reads `pullRequestId` and `artifactVersionId` as null. Principals are worker principals, which are not scoped to one organization, so they carry no composite foreign key.

tables.name: review_findings
tables.purpose: Structured deduplicated review issues, one row per fingerprint of a cycle
tables.constraints: Immutable evidence: SELECT and INSERT only, `created_at` and no `updated_at` or `version`. UNIQUE(review_cycle_id,fingerprint); UNIQUE(organization_id,id); FK(organization_id,review_cycle_id) to review_cycles(organization_id,id) cascades. `fingerprint` is the worker-computed lowercase SHA-256 of the normalized path, category and title, with no line number, so the same issue keeps its fingerprint across cycles; the server checks the format and uniqueness and recomputes `blocking` from `severity` (blocker and major block). `line` is null or from 1 to 2147483647 (a Postgres `integer`); `path` and `body` are bounded (200 and 500 characters), not blank and free of U+0000 and lone surrogates. A finding row is never marked resolved or withdrawn: the `ReviewFinding.status` projection is derived on read, `open` exactly when the fingerprint is reported by the run's latest cycle (highest ordinal), otherwise `resolved`, so a finding that a middle cycle repeated but the latest cycle dropped reads `resolved` in every earlier cycle; `withdrawn` has no writer. `resolution_artifact_id` and `remote_comment_id` are omitted and read null until remote review comments exist. Unresolved blockers and majors block delivery; the implementer cannot dismiss a finding to pass.

tables.name: delivery_decisions
tables.purpose: The bounded proceed, repair or stop decision taken after a review, with the facts it was taken from
tables.constraints: Immutable evidence: SELECT and INSERT only, `created_at` and no `updated_at` or `version`. UNIQUE(organization_id,run_id,ordinal) numbers the run's decisions from 0, so the newest decision is the highest ordinal and a replayed result cannot add a second decision for one review. `review_cycle_id` is null only for a review job that failed (`reviewer_unavailable` for fault `REVIEWER_UNAVAILABLE`, `review_failed` for any other fault), which produced no cycle. The decision and its reason are vocabulary enforced in TypeScript, and each reason belongs to exactly one decision (`clean` proceeds, `repair_selected` repairs, every other reason stops). `failed_checks` lists the required checks that failed on the judged head as `{checkRunId, checkId, result, reason, exitCode}`, the evidence a repair receives; `blocking_fingerprints` lists the fingerprints of the review's blocking findings; `limits` freezes `{maxRepairCycles, maxLoopDurationMs, maxFindings}` as they stood for the run. A stop decision is paired with a pre-failed `delivery_gate` run step whose error names the decision. UNIQUE(organization_id,id); FK(organization_id,run_id) to workflow_runs(organization_id,id) and FK(organization_id,review_cycle_id) to review_cycles(organization_id,id) cascade. A decision is never an approval: the delivery gate reads the newest decision and re-reads the required checks, so a later failed check row blocks a candidate an earlier `proceed` let through.

tables.name: check_runs
tables.purpose: Deterministic check results bound to the exact candidate and its pull request metadata
tables.constraints: Immutable evidence: the application role holds SELECT and INSERT only, so a row is never updated or deleted, carries `created_at` and has no `updated_at` or `version`. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; FK(organization_id,run_id) to workflow_runs(organization_id,id) cascades with the run and FK(organization_id,evidence_version_id) to artifact_versions(organization_id,id) is the classified retained-evidence reference, so a retained check row protects its evidence bytes from collection. Partial UNIQUE(organization_id,job_id,fence,check_id) where job_id is not null records each check once per job attempt fence; metadata rows (commits, title, description, merge_message) carry no job, attempt or fence and repeat across evaluations, newest first. `run_step_id`, `job_id` and `attempt_id` are provenance written by the result transaction without foreign keys. Each row stores the head, base, profile, effective policy, subject, checker, title, body, merge-message and commit-selection digests it was observed under; a column is null when the check does not depend on that identity. `result` is `passed` only for a verified process exit or a satisfied rule, `failed` means the check ran and did not pass, and `unavailable` (missing tool, checker, metadata or revision, unbound rule, skipped) blocks a required check exactly like `failed` without being reported as one. `pull_request_id` is omitted until a run has a pull request (#97): `pull_requests` has a table now, but no writer sets this reference. Required check names come from the pinned repository profile; the exact tested head/base/policy must match the delivery candidate. Tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization.

tables.name: merge_entries
tables.purpose: Serialized merge coordination
tables.constraints: At most one merging entry per repository/target; rebase creates new SHA and invalidates previous review/check evidence. Each entry has 1..100 merge_entry_checks, validated with its review under one locked transaction; run/repository/head/base/policy match and checks pass with no blocking findings. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: merge_entry_checks
tables.purpose: Exact check evidence retained for a merge candidate
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(merge_entry_id,check_run_id); both FKs ON DELETE RESTRICT; linked evidence must match entry run/head/base/policy in its creation transaction. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: deployments
tables.purpose: Release, health verification and rollback
tables.constraints: Only merged tested revision; same environment serialized; rollback records new effect referencing previous immutable release. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: event_clock
tables.purpose: Commit-ordered durable event cursor
tables.constraints: One row per organization and stream; sequence allocation is atomic with domain-event insertion. Domain-event sequence values are unique within their organization and never disclose another tenant's write activity.

tables.name: application_migration_drain
tables.purpose: Crash-recoverable application connection drain for incompatible data cutovers
tables.constraints: At most the database singleton row exists. Its transactionally persisted ACL snapshot makes connection revocation recoverable after process failure; bakery_app has no access.

tables.name: domain_events
tables.purpose: Durable client-visible changes
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(sequence) remains compatibility-only for mixed-version storage and is never exposed as a cursor; UNIQUE(organization_id,organization_sequence) is the canonical tenant-local event order. Payload is a bounded safe projection; authorization applies during replay and live broadcast. Conversation changes populate conversation_id even before task creation. Scope filtering always intersects live resource authorization; broad application/repository subscriptions cannot expose narrower conversation or task content. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception. Issue 59 adds nullable organization-constrained worker_host_id and worker_enrollment_id scope references so worker/enrollment subscriptions authorize before any task exists; public payloads contain references/versions, not tokens or provider responses.

tables.name: outbox
tables.purpose: Dispatch acknowledged domain events
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(destination,delivery_key); transactional insert with domain mutation; repeated dispatch uses same provider/event id. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: idempotency_records
tables.purpose: HTTP/MCP mutation dedupe
tables.constraints: organization scope requires organization_id; installation scope requires it null and is limited to explicit installation-admin operations. UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT(scope,organization_id,principal_id,operation,key). Same key and changed digest returns IDEMPOTENCY_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH; replay still rechecks current authority. in_progress is published only with durable intent. Completed rows require response_status, response_body and response_headers together; response_status is the registered successful HTTP status, response_body is bounded UTF-8 JSON bytes, and response_headers is a bounded object containing only content-type, location and etag with safe values. In-progress rows keep all response fields null.

tables.name: external_effects
tables.purpose: Immutable external side-effect intent, delivery and reconciliation ledger
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(organization_id,operation,target,idempotency_key). Request digest covers the request identity only: operation, action version, target, connection, resource, external account and resource identities, validated input, actor, run step, automation, reservation and approval reference. It deliberately excludes authority version counters (authorization revision, install, grant, manifest digest), so an unrelated grant edit never turns a replay into a mismatch; claim rechecks all of them against fresh authority (and the broker rechecks the grant again before send). Changed input/resource is IDEMPOTENCY_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH. Integration effects require connection, resource, action_version, immutable external identities and authorization revision; MCP/deployment effects retain their existing connection/profile provenance without fake integration IDs. Subscription deliveries require subscription and integration provenance. One executor claims a dispatch generation. Unknown results reconcile with the same immutable identity and current grant; absence alone never authorizes another write. Safe arguments/results are bounded (64 KiB) but not redacted by the ledger: secrets stay out because action input schemas carry no credential fields and the broker refuses any response that echoes a credential. A result over the bound is stored as null (the remote id is kept). UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception. Credential provenance may reference a same-organization secret version OR an installation-owned version whose installation matches this effect’s authorized integration connection. The broker checks that explicit exception under the effect/credential locks; no arbitrary cross-organization credential reference is allowed. Migration 0127 persists this table: the status state machine, bounds and the integration-effect non-null invariant are enforced in TypeScript (no CHECK constraints); identity columns are immutable via column-scoped grants. Migration 0135 adds FK(organization_id,integration_connection_id) to integration_connections(organization_id,id) and FK(integration_resource_id,integration_connection_id) to integration_resources(id,connection_id), both NO ACTION, so an effect keeps its connection and that connection's resource across suspend, revoke and reconnect. MCP connection, automation, subscription, install and grant columns have no foreign key until their parent tables exist; integration_install_id names the integration gate's deployed install, not an integration_installations row. credential_version_id is unwritten until credential provenance (#60). All parent references are ON DELETE NO ACTION except the organization cascade; budget_reservations.external_effect_id references this table.

tables.name: audit_events
tables.purpose: Redacted actor/action outcome trail
tables.constraints: Append-only; no prompts/credentials; Admin read; separate retention from short-lived streams. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: usage_records
tables.purpose: Measured and estimated provider usage with explicit provenance, authenticated replay authority, and retention independent of workflow history or artifact export
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(organization_id,usage_fact_id) and UNIQUE(organization_id,provider,billing_account_id,provider_call_id); unknown is never coerced to zero; only provider-authoritative rows with an exact immutable provider receipt contribute to known cost; legacy and worker-asserted measured rows remain worker-unverified and are exposed separately; known settlement updates both installation-month and run-lifetime ledgers in one transaction; unknown facts retain both holds; canonical digest binds the receipt to authenticated worker authority and frozen billing pins; usage facts survive workflow-history and artifact-export expiry.

tables.name: evaluation_definitions
tables.purpose: Versioned score or deterministic evaluator
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(slug,revision); registered code evaluator or configured Mastra scorer; no untrusted arbitrary code in YAML. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: evaluation_cases
tables.purpose: Sanitized replay corpus
tables.constraints: Immutable corpus revision; no secret-bearing real transcripts; use the same schema in offline and online scoring. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: evaluation_runs
tables.purpose: Pinned evaluation batch or online sample
tables.constraints: Online model scores observational unless explicit versioned delivery policy requires that evaluator. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: evaluation_results
tables.purpose: Individual measured score and evidence
tables.constraints: Exactly one case or subject artifact; failure is not score zero; keep evaluator/model/corpus provenance through run. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: worker_enrollments
tables.purpose: One-use worker bootstrap
tables.constraints: UNIQUE token_hash; 10 minute default; consume atomically; enrollment token never appears in normal logs or GET responses. Registration locks this row and requires normalized requested capabilities to be a subset of allowed_capabilities; consume only in the successful host/principal transaction. State is derived from consumed_at/canceled_at/expires_at (pending, consumed, canceled, expired); the locked register/cancel transaction decides the winner when registration races cancel or replacement, and snapshot/replay resolves the true machine. Replacements copy the predecessor's intent, atomically cancel a still-pending predecessor and never reissue a usable token for a consumed enrollment; an expired predecessor remains an expired audit record. Re-pair enrollments bind the exact same-organization revoked host and its expected credential generation and rotate the generation on consumption without transferring organization. worker_host_id is assigned on successful consumption. No normal response contains the token hash. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: worker_commands
tables.purpose: Durable steering and cancellation delivery
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(attempt_id,message_id) for steering; heartbeat returns pending commands until acked; terminal acknowledged/rejected rows are compacted into worker_command_ack_tombstones, whose compact status/time record is retained for exact duplicate acknowledgement after the command row is swept. Partial UNIQUE(attempt_id,kind) WHERE kind=cancel; repeated cancel returns the existing command. Server commands are steer/follow_up/cancel only; start is a claim assignment and shutdown is a local supervisor action. UNIQUE(organization_id,id) supports composite foreign keys; tenant-owned parent references are constrained to the same organization unless this record documents a host-owned exception.

tables.name: worker_command_ack_tombstones
tables.purpose: Compact durable command acknowledgement replay
tables.constraints: PRIMARY KEY(command_id); exact host-scoped duplicate acknowledgements remain retrievable only until expires_at, then batched retention collection removes them; tombstones contain no command payload or credential. UNIQUE(organization_id,command_id) supports the tenant-scoped command identity; index(expires_at,command_id) bounds collection.

tables.name: worker_components
tables.purpose: Bounded machine inventory of installed and available components
tables.constraints: UNIQUE(worker_host_id,component_key); one row per host component from the latest accepted inventory report; changing inventory increments the host inventory revision.
